name: Mass and excitation: fixed-truth exploratory pilot

aims: Map how positive-mass accuracy and conditional interval coverage depend jointly on true mass, excitation and the number of stable repeated readings.
Verify the reusable experiment workflow and estimate the cost and fixed replication count of a subsequent study; do not select an overall winning estimator from this pilot.
data_generating_mechanisms: Newton II is assumed correct: latent force equals positive true mass times latent acceleration, with a common direction [1,0,0]. Direction is used only by the simulator.

True masses 0.25, 1 and 4 are crossed with per-reading acceleration SNR 0, 0.5, 2 and 8. Force is derived from mass times acceleration. Each channel has known independent Gaussian component noise with standard deviation 1.

Separate experiments use n=1 and n=4 independent readings of the same unchanged latent pair. Estimators receive the sample means and known mean standard deviations 1/sqrt(n). No changing excitation or shared estimated calibration is modeled.

R=512 independent simulated experiments are generated per cell. Training noise is shared across the cells within each n experiment; the two n experiments use distinct random seeds. Held-out observations use independent random streams.
estimands: The fixed positive physical mass m in force-units/acceleration-units, varied independently of latent excitation.
For each method and each cell separately: repeated-experiment expected bounded point loss and probability of factor-two failure.
For each flat and tube conditional mass law separately: repeated-experiment coverage of its central 95% interval at the stipulated fixed mass.
methods: Evaluate every method already supplied by the configured comparison engine on the same observations within each cell; record its existing method metadata. The repeated-reading engine may include additional covariance-aware and RMS-approximation baselines.
Preserve the flat joint mass point E[f]/E[alpha] and the Newton-II premise. No law-rejection gate is introduced.
Evaluate flat and tube conditional probability laws separately from their point summaries. Deterministic baselines are not assigned invented uncertainty intervals.
Use existing numerical refinement checks. A failed numerical experiment remains explicitly failed; completed trial counts are never substituted for planned counts.
performance_measures: Primary point loss: min(log(m_hat/m)^2, log(2)^2), with invalid estimates assigned the cap. Primary factor-two failure: m_hat outside [m/2,2m], including invalid estimates.

Primary uncertainty measure: 95% central interval coverage for each of the flat and tube laws. Monte Carlo precision targets are 0.005 for capped loss and coverage and 0.01 for factor-two failure; these are planning targets, not stopping rules.
Report paired flat-minus-comparator point differences and their directly calculated paired MCSEs. Do not approximate paired uncertainty from independent-method standard errors.
Retain existing secondary losses, interval widths, scores, invalid-output counts and numerical diagnostics. Ordinary MCSE interpretation for unbounded scores requires the relevant moments to exist.
Use all attempted trials under the declared failure policy. Inapplicable zero-denominator relative force-prediction scores remain explicitly unavailable.

methodology.title: Morris, White and Crowther: Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods (ADEMP and Monte Carlo uncertainty)
Chipman and Bingham: Planning and interpreting simulation studies with design and analysis of experiments (factor interactions)
Pawel et al.: Handling Missingness, Failures, and Non-Convergence in Simulation Studies (failure-aware evaluation)

interpretation: Exploratory pilot only: report cell-specific evidence and uncertainty, without a global winner or a confirmatory performance claim.

The number of readings n within an experiment is distinct from the number R of independent simulated experiments. Increasing n changes the measurement problem; increasing R reduces Monte Carlo uncertainty.

At zero excitation, force and acceleration truth are both zero but mass remains a stipulated positive estimand. With the declared mass-independent measurement noise, the observation distribution is identical for every true mass: this experiment contains no information about mass. Distinct fixed-mass scores are assessments against different stipulated truths, not evidence that the data distinguish those masses.
Repeated-experiment interval coverage is a property to measure. Nominal 95% conditional probability does not guarantee 95% fixed-truth coverage.
Keep all 512 trials per cell regardless of apparent performance or precision. Do not stop early or automatically extend a run. A later study should predeclare its fixed R and use fresh seeds.

Pilot-variance R calculations are uncertain, especially if no failures occur. Also report conservative bounded-variance planning values. Neither number is a simultaneous-confidence guarantee across all methods and cells.

Checkpointing is at completed-experiment granularity. Resume verifies the normalized specification, source hashes, runtime versions and completed output hashes. An incomplete experiment restarts in a fresh attempt directory; earlier partial output is retained.
